n: Four documents, all dated Thursday. The first is from Google. It says the company is partnering with Blue Origin on the first heavy-lift launch for Project Suncatcher, its long-term effort to run AI computing in orbit on solar power. The launch is targeted for the first quarter of 2029, and each satellite has roughly the capacity of one data center rack. The second is from Amazon Web Services. It says AI agents can now find and buy select products in its marketplace and pay per request in US dollars, and that customers can set spending limits and approved sellers before agents transact. The third is from Google. It says its Gemini app can now work through Mac apps and websites in the background to finish repetitive tasks, on Apple Silicon Macs, for personal accounts 18 and older on its paid plans. The fourth, also from Google, puts a feature called Tool Retrieval in preview for developers: an agent connected to hundreds of tools loads the details of a tool only when it needs them. What it means for your work: two of these four are about software that acts for you, one that clicks through your computer and one that spends money. Both documents name the controls, a background window you can watch and a spending limit you set first. Before you turn on anything that acts for you, find the limit and set it yourself.

sources.title: Google: a 2029 launch is planned for its AI computing satellites
